notes: Spokes of the story web (revision 6: The Siege reads the forward war outlook, The Famine the seasonal food model, and victors have The Spoils, The Veteran, The Peace and The Pursuit). History casts and personality tilts: boosts read facts from the record and the world, the archetype and claim fits are modest multipliers, and the two personality spokes (The Absolute, The Ascension) carry no claim fit so they only win when the log is quiet. `requires` is a list of conjunctions over facts the compiler derives from a hero record and the world (`story_web.facts.FACTS`); a leading `!` negates. `pull` is the alignment prior that places the spoke on the web and weights fit; it never clamps. `fits` names archetypes that multiply the weight; `claims` names claim verbs that multiply it; `cast` says whether people, Dreads or both may walk the spoke. Each act has one prompt, one completion predicate, one abandonment predicate and two to four typed options carrying a bounded alignment delta. `examples` are prose and are never evaluated.

tropes.name: Revenge

acts.title: The wound
acts.prompt: Find me proof of who did this to {lost}, and where {rival} stands now.

options.text: Find a witness in {rival}'s own city.
Recover what was left in the ruins of {lost}.
Ask whether the wound is worth reopening.

acts.title: The reckoning
acts.prompt: Bring me to {rival}.

options.text: Stay {hero}'s hand at the last moment.
Insist it be settled openly, by the old forms.

acts.title: The empty ledger
acts.prompt: It is done. Tell me what I am for now.

options.text: Point {hero} at an open mantle of their people.
Let {hero} walk away from all of it.

examples: The proof shows the credited actor was not the actual one, and the hero is recast into Unmasking.
The rival is spared; the hero gains rival:spared and rests with a Redemption hook.

tropes.name: Redemption

acts.title: The ledger
acts.prompt: There is a debt in my name. Help me pay it where it was made.

options.text: Pay the debt without a name attached.

acts.title: The shortcut
acts.prompt: I know a faster way. Stop me if you have to.

options.text: Refuse the shortcut and find the slow road.

acts.title: The witness
acts.prompt: Someone remembers what I was. Let me face them.

options.text: Speak for {hero} before the one they wronged.
Let {hero} stand alone and take the answer.

examples: Forgiven, the hero's claim becomes protect and they rest with a Succession hook as a mentor.
The shortcut is taken and drift reverses; the hero is recast into Temptation.

tropes.name: Fall

acts.title: The slight
acts.prompt: They took what was mine. Help me take something back.

options.text: Turn it into a claim for restitution instead.

acts.title: The accomplice
acts.prompt: Do this one thing and do not ask what it is for.

options.text: Find out what it is really for first.

acts.title: The seat
acts.prompt: Now help me hold it.

options.text: Defend the seized holding at {hero}'s side.

examples: The raid becomes restitution and the hero is recast into Redemption.
The seat is held and the hero rests with a Tyranny hook.

tropes.name: Reclamation

acts.title: The ruin
acts.prompt: Go to what was ours at {lost}. Tell me what is left.

options.text: Scout the ruin and report what holds it.

acts.title: The claim
acts.prompt: Clear it, and I will bring my people.

options.text: Tell {hero} the living home matters more than the dead one.

acts.title: The founding
acts.prompt: Stand with me when they come to take {lost} back.

options.text: Hold the resettlement against its old enemy.
Crush dissent inside the walls first.

examples: The ruin is a Dread's lair and the hero is recast into The Hunt.
Held harshly, the hero rests with a Tyranny hook.

tropes.name: Homecoming

acts.title: The wall
acts.prompt: {home} took us in. Help me make it safe.

acts.title: The old banner
acts.prompt: Someone from before has come. Find out what they want.

options.text: Help {hero} refuse the old people's summons.

acts.title: The choice
acts.prompt: Both places need me tonight. Choose for me.

examples: The old realm sends for the hero and they are recast into Reclamation.
The new home is saved and the hero rests as its warden.

tropes.name: Usurpation

acts.title: The faction
acts.prompt: The seat is weak. Help me find who else thinks so.

options.text: Sound out the realm's other notables.
Buy the camps and remnants outside the walls.

acts.title: The stroke
acts.prompt: Tonight. Be at the gate.

options.text: Force a challenge by the old forms instead.

acts.title: The crown
acts.prompt: They say I am not the rightful one. Prove them wrong, or quiet them.

examples: The stroke fails and the hero is recast onto Exile's Road.
The council is removed and the hero rests with a Tyranny hook.

tropes.name: Tyranny

acts.title: The census
acts.prompt: Find the ones who still speak against me.

acts.title: The heir
acts.prompt: My own blood conspires. Bring them to me.

acts.title: The mirror
acts.prompt: Stand beside me when they come.

options.text: Open the gate to the rebels.

examples: The player warns the dissenters and is cast as an ally in a Rebellion.
The tyrant wins and the realm gains realm:tyrant, seeding Rebellion entries for others.

tropes.name: Rebellion

acts.title: The spark
acts.prompt: Show them the tyrant can bleed.

options.text: Free a prisoner from the tyrant's cells.
Burn the census and whoever guards it.

acts.title: The camp
acts.prompt: We have a cause. Get us an army.

options.text: Ask a rival realm for soldiers.
Carry the tyrant's offer of terms to {hero}.

acts.title: The fall of the seat
acts.prompt: Open the gate.

examples: Innocents die in the spark and the hero is recast into Fall.
The hero takes the seat and rests with a Usurpation hook.

tropes.name: The Hunt

acts.title: The trail
acts.prompt: {rival} has been seen. Find the lair.

options.text: Bait it with a hamlet's herd.

acts.title: The cost
acts.prompt: I need one thing before I face it.

options.text: Earn the ward or relic honestly.
Take it from whoever holds it.

acts.title: The lair
acts.prompt: Come with me, or hold the door.

options.text: Hold the door and let {hero} go in alone.

examples: The Dread is long-lived and speaks; the hero is recast into The Bargain.
The hero dies and the Dread lives; a mantle opens for the player.

tropes.name: The Bargain

acts.title: The terms
acts.prompt: It will talk. Carry its words.

options.text: Negotiate a boundary between lair and town.
Refuse to bargain with it at all.

acts.title: The breach
acts.prompt: Someone has crossed the line. Find out who.

options.text: Find the camp encroaching on the range.
Ask whether the Dread lied about the breach.

acts.title: The keeping
acts.prompt: Hold the line for both sides.

options.text: Warden the boundary through the season.
Let the town break the terms.

examples: Peace persists and the hero rests with a Warden's Line hook.
The town breaks the terms and the Dread's next city makes an Obsessed Hunter.

tropes.name: Unmasking

acts.title: The favour
acts.prompt: You saved my life. Let me repay it.

options.text: Check what the task actually does first.

acts.title: The pattern
acts.prompt: One more. The valley is still sick.

options.text: Find an honest witness to the first result.

acts.title: The face
acts.prompt: You know. So now you choose.

options.text: Show the hidden goal was benign after all.

examples: Exposed and driven out, the hero is recast into Fall.
The hidden goal proves benign; the hero gains stake:regained and rests with a Redemption hook.

tropes.name: Betrayal

acts.title: The offer
acts.prompt: Carry a message to the other side. Quietly.

acts.title: The price
acts.prompt: They want proof of loyalty.

acts.title: The reckoning
acts.prompt: They know. Get me out, or stand with me.

options.text: Argue for mercy when {hero} is caught.

examples: The hero escapes to the new side and rests with a Usurpation hook.
Caught, and spared at the player's word, the hero gains rival:spared.

tropes.name: Crusade

acts.title: The sign
acts.prompt: The heavens have spoken. Bring the word to the next town.

options.text: Carry the word and feed the listeners.

acts.title: The rival faith
acts.prompt: Their shrine stands on our ground.

acts.title: The silence
acts.prompt: The heavens are quiet. Tell me I was right.

options.text: Take {hero} to the nearest theophany site.
Tell {hero} the silence is the answer.

examples: A massacre at the rival shrine; the hero rests with a Tyranny hook.
No sign comes and the hero is recast into Redemption or Exile's Road.

tropes.name: Temptation

acts.title: The whisper
acts.prompt: The ground here answers me. Help me learn why.

options.text: Show {hero} a way to suppress it.

acts.title: The use
acts.prompt: Once. To save them. Then never again.

options.text: Let {hero} use the taint against the threat.
Find another way to meet the threat.

acts.title: The mask slips
acts.prompt: Bind me, or follow me.

examples: Suppressed with help; the hero is recast into The Warden's Line.
Embraced; the claim becomes exploit on the node and the hero rests with a Fall hook.

tropes.name: Succession

acts.title: The test
acts.prompt: Take my successor into the field. Do not help them.

acts.title: The doom
acts.prompt: I am dying. Do not tell them.

options.text: Keep the secret and finish the errand.

acts.title: The passing
acts.prompt: Bring them to me.

options.text: Bring the successor for the last meeting.
Ask {hero} to pass the mantle to you instead.

examples: The heir fails badly and the mentor takes the player on; recast into Inheritance.
The mantle passes and the mentor becomes legend.

tropes.name: Inheritance

acts.title: The relic
acts.prompt: {relic} rests in the ruin. Take it up or leave it.

acts.title: The predecessor's enemy
acts.prompt: The one they never finished with still lives.

options.text: Hear the rival's side of the story.

acts.title: The claim
acts.prompt: Finish what they started, or finish it your way.

options.text: Finish the claim exactly as it was left.

examples: The rival tells the other side; the legend is recast into Unmasking posthumously.
Finished as left, the hero becomes legend and the next heir gains legend:predecessor.

tropes.name: Sacrifice

acts.title: The threat
acts.prompt: They are coming and I cannot stop them alone.

options.text: Gather what fighters can be found.

acts.title: The cost
acts.prompt: Someone has to hold the pass.

options.text: Find a way that spares everyone.

acts.title: The stand
acts.prompt: Go. Do not look back.

examples: The hero dies and the stake survives; a mantle opens.
The player finds a way that spares everyone; recast into The Warden's Line.

tropes.name: The Warden's Line

acts.title: The post
acts.prompt: The ward was tested again. Find what tested it.

options.text: Ask whether the realm itself is moving the line.

acts.title: The relief
acts.prompt: I asked for relief. None came. Go ask why.

options.text: Tell {hero} to walk away from the post.

acts.title: The breach
acts.prompt: It is through. Hold with me.

options.text: Fall back and warn the towns.

examples: The realm is moving the line; the hero is recast into Rebellion.
The breach is held and the hero rests at the post.

tropes.name: Exile's Road

acts.title: The road
acts.prompt: I have nowhere. Let me travel with you a while.

options.text: Find {hero} a settlement that will take them.

acts.title: The pursuit
acts.prompt: They will not stop. Help me end it or lose them.

acts.title: The return
acts.prompt: I could go back. Tell me if I should.

examples: A settlement offers shelter and the hero is recast into Homecoming.
The hero returns and rests with a Reclamation or Revenge hook.

tropes.name: The Vow

acts.title: The letter
acts.prompt: The charter says one thing. Read it to me again.

options.text: Retrieve the charter and read it aloud.
Argue for the oath's spirit over its letter.

acts.title: The cost
acts.prompt: Keeping it will hurt someone. Help me see who.

options.text: Name who the oath will harm.
Tell {hero} the oath comes first regardless.

acts.title: The keeping
acts.prompt: I will keep it. Stand where I can see you.

examples: A warden closes a pass against refugees and keeps the vow.
The player stops the keeping; the oath is broken and the hero is recast into Fall.

tropes.name: The Regency

acts.title: The debt
acts.prompt: The sovereign owes me. Collect it quietly.

options.text: Warn the sovereign what is being collected.

acts.title: The rival
acts.prompt: Someone else has the sovereign's ear.

acts.title: The choice
acts.prompt: The seat will empty. Help me choose who sits.

options.text: Seat the one who would rule well.

examples: A chancellor runs a puppet sovereign.
The regent is exposed by a Trickster's jest and recast into Fall.

tropes.name: The Strings

acts.title: The ceremony
acts.prompt: Attend me. Say nothing the chancellor would not.

options.text: Say the thing the chancellor would not.

acts.title: The doubt
acts.prompt: Tell me what you saw. Not what he told you.

options.text: Tell the sovereign what was withheld.

acts.title: The cut
acts.prompt: If I refuse him, will anyone stand with me?

options.text: Stand with the sovereign against the adviser.
Advise the sovereign to keep the strings.

examples: A sovereign finds courage and is recast into Rebellion against their own court.
The strings are cut and the sovereign hangs.

tropes.name: The Design

acts.title: The fallback
acts.prompt: Do this, and if it fails, this.

options.text: Do neither and see what {hero} does.

acts.title: The variable
acts.prompt: Something I did not model. Find out what.

acts.title: The end state
acts.prompt: Now the last piece.

options.text: Break the design at the end.

examples: The unmodelled variable is the player.
The plan completes with the player as the useful piece.

tropes.name: The Skim

acts.title: The invoice
acts.prompt: A shipment went missing. Find it before the audit.

options.text: Forge the paperwork that explains it.

acts.title: The equal
acts.prompt: A new merchant undercuts me. Learn their price.

acts.title: The fire
acts.prompt: The ledger has to burn. Or the auditor does.

options.text: Bring the ledger to the auditor.

examples: A crooked steward funds an orphanage.
One sells the city's granary during a famine and is recast into The Trial.

tropes.name: The Monopoly

acts.title: The deficit
acts.prompt: Their granary is short. Confirm the number.

options.text: Count the shortfall at the neighbouring core.
Report it larger than it is.

acts.title: The squeeze
acts.prompt: Close the second road.

options.text: Block or buy the second route.
Keep the road open and tell the seat.

acts.title: The price
acts.prompt: Now they buy from me. Carry the terms.

examples: A magnate feeds a famine at a fair price and is remembered.
One buys a city and seeds a Rebellion.

tropes.name: The Chronicle

acts.title: The retelling
acts.prompt: Tell the story as they know it, where I can hear.

options.text: Retell the credited deed in the hall.
Ask the awkward question in the hall.

acts.title: The witness
acts.prompt: Someone was there. Find out what they remember.

acts.title: The record
acts.prompt: The chronicle holds, or it does not. Decide.

options.text: Pay the actual actor for silence.

examples: A hero confesses and walks Redemption.
One silences the witness and walks Fall.

tropes.name: The Pardon

acts.title: The terms
acts.prompt: I let {rival} live. Make sure they know why.

options.text: Carry them as a threat instead.

acts.title: The relapse
acts.prompt: They did it again. Find out if it is true.

options.text: Confirm or disprove the new deed.

acts.title: The second chance
acts.prompt: One more. Then no more.

examples: The rival becomes an ally and later a Turncoat.
A Forgiving who is right about people too late.

tropes.name: The Cage

acts.title: The rules
acts.prompt: When it comes out, you leave. Agree to that.

acts.title: The pack
acts.prompt: Someone I love is near it now. Get them clear.

options.text: Move the ally out of reach.
Use the ally to draw it out.

acts.title: The use
acts.prompt: Point it at something that deserves it.

options.text: Point it at a real threat.
Point it at whoever is convenient.

examples: A rage kills a Dread.
A rage kills the pack and opens Revenge for someone else.

tropes.name: The Two Faces

acts.title: The gap
acts.prompt: I promised you something. Which of us said it?

options.text: Hold {hero} to the first face's promise.

acts.title: The other
acts.prompt: She told you things. Tell me what.

options.text: Pass the fact between the faces.
Keep each face ignorant of the other.

acts.title: The conflict
acts.prompt: Both claims cannot hold. Pick one and hold me to it.

examples: A hero whose two civilizations go to war.
A mage of two schools whose second face strengthens the node the first suppresses.

tropes.name: The Answer

acts.title: The question
acts.prompt: You want the dangerous half. Prove you can carry the safe half.

options.text: Do the safe task at the node without changing its school.
Push for the dangerous half now.

acts.title: The use
acts.prompt: Someone used what I taught. Find out who.

acts.title: The half
acts.prompt: Here is the rest. Remember I said no.

examples: A sage whose answer builds a Well.
One whose answer ends a Blight.

tropes.name: The Absolute

acts.title: The statute
acts.prompt: Here is the law of this place. Carry it to the next.

acts.title: The exception
acts.prompt: They ask me to bend. I cannot. Tell them.

acts.title: The test
acts.prompt: Now the corner costs me everything. Watch.

options.text: Watch and let the cost fall.

examples: A lawful-good absolute lets a city fall rather than lie.
A chaotic-evil one burns their own hall for the joke of it.

tropes.name: The Ascension

acts.title: The following
acts.prompt: They are beginning to watch. Show them something.

acts.title: The mismatch
acts.prompt: This realm is the wrong shape for me. Change it.

acts.title: The remaking
acts.prompt: Convert them, or replace them.

examples: A benevolent legend founds a faith.
A malevolent one the realm misidentifies until too late.

tropes.name: The Jest

acts.title: The target
acts.prompt: Who is the biggest name within a day's walk?

options.text: Name the highest-fame notable in reach.

acts.title: The setup
acts.prompt: Get me into their hall.

acts.title: The punchline
acts.prompt: Tomorrow at dawn. Bring everyone.

options.text: Make it a jest everyone survives.
Let the punchline end at the gallows.

examples: A jest unseats a Kingmaker.
One ends with someone hanged.

tropes.name: The Schism

acts.title: The text
acts.prompt: The mother faith has it wrong. Find the proof at the old shrine.

options.text: Visit the old shrine and bring back the proof.

acts.title: The congregation
acts.prompt: Bring me ten who will listen.

acts.title: The break
acts.prompt: They will name me heretic. Let them.

examples: A schism becomes a Crusade.
One dies as a cult in a ruin.

tropes.name: The Founding

acts.title: The site
acts.prompt: There is good ground two days out. Walk it with me.

options.text: Take ground someone else already holds.

acts.title: The first winter
acts.prompt: We will not last the season without help.

options.text: Bring supplies from the nearest core.

acts.title: The charter
acts.prompt: Name it. Then defend it.

options.text: Write the charter and defend the site.

examples: A camp becomes a hamlet.
A founding fails and leaves a new ruin, and a new hook.

tropes.name: The Siege

acts.title: The walls
acts.prompt: They are coming. Help me count what we have.

acts.title: The sally
acts.prompt: One strike before they close the ring.

acts.title: The gate
acts.prompt: Hold it.

options.text: Open the gate to the enemy.

examples: A siege held makes a Warlord.
One lost makes a Pretender.

tropes.name: The Famine

acts.title: The count
acts.prompt: The granary is short. Tell me by how much.

acts.title: The road
acts.prompt: The next core has surplus. Open the road.

acts.title: The choice
acts.prompt: Feed the city or the hamlets. Not both.

examples: A famine makes a Magnate rich.
One makes a Tyrant of a good sovereign.

tropes.name: The Blight

acts.title: The sign
acts.prompt: The crops turn and the moon is wrong. Find the source.

options.text: Trace the sickness to its node.

acts.title: The suppression
acts.prompt: Weaken it, if you can.

options.text: Flood it with the opposing school.

acts.title: The recovery
acts.prompt: It is fading. Make sure nothing else grows in its place.

options.text: Watch the region through the season.

examples: A blight cured makes a Benevolent.
One cured with the wrong school overshoots.

tropes.name: The Binding

acts.title: The approach
acts.prompt: It is hostile to me now. Get me close enough to speak.

options.text: Refuse to bring a necromancer near it.

acts.title: The bind
acts.prompt: Hold the ward while I work.

options.text: Drop the ward at the crucial moment.

acts.title: The use
acts.prompt: Now it works for us. Give it a task.

examples: A necromancer staffs a fortress.
One whose binding breaks during a Siege.

tropes.name: The Domain

acts.title: The anchor
acts.prompt: The key point can be built on. Bring the recipe.

options.text: Warn the neighbours what is being built.

acts.title: The attunement
acts.prompt: It needs a school. Choose with me.

options.text: Attune it to balance the region.

acts.title: The border
acts.prompt: The neighbours have noticed. Meet them at the line.

examples: A Well ends a Blight.
A domain starts a war.

tropes.name: The Delve

acts.title: The map
acts.prompt: {relic} rests where {lost} fell. Learn the way in.

options.text: Buy a map from the camp that squats there.

acts.title: The descent
acts.prompt: Go. I will wait at the gate.

options.text: Go down and bring it back.
Bring it back and keep it.

acts.title: The return
acts.prompt: Now decide who keeps it.

options.text: Place it with a site or a sovereign.

examples: A delve arms an Inherited Hero.
One hands a focus to a Deceiver.

tropes.name: The Alliance

acts.title: The envoy
acts.prompt: Carry my terms to {realm_other}. Come back with theirs.

acts.title: The price
acts.prompt: They want a marriage, a road, or a hostage. Advise me.

acts.title: The seal
acts.prompt: Witness it.

options.text: Sell the terms to a third realm.

examples: An alliance prevents a Siege.
One that a Turncoat sells.

tropes.name: The Lair

options.text: Hunt at the edge of the range.
Sleep and let the range be.

examples: A Dread becomes an Ancient.
One whose second city makes an Obsessed Hunter.

tropes.name: The Trial

acts.title: The charge
acts.prompt: They say I did it. Find who says so.

acts.title: The evidence
acts.prompt: Bring what proves it, or what disproves it.

options.text: Bring the evidence as it is.

acts.title: The verdict
acts.prompt: Stand with me when they read it.

examples: A wrongful verdict makes a Rebel.
A rightful one begins Redemption.

tropes.name: The Court

acts.title: The seat
acts.prompt: My seat is watched. Find out by whom.

acts.title: The favour
acts.prompt: The sovereign asks something of my office. Help me answer.

options.text: Serve it and keep a share.

acts.title: The succession
acts.prompt: The seat above mine may empty. Tell me who is ready.

options.text: Name the one who would rule well.

examples: A magistrate who becomes a Kingmaker.
A market steward whose share becomes The Skim.

tropes.name: The Reign

acts.title: The petition
acts.prompt: The hall is full of petitions. Hear one for me and tell me the truth of it.

options.text: Sell the sovereign's ear to the petitioner.

acts.title: The council
acts.prompt: One of my council lies to me. Which?

acts.title: The succession
acts.prompt: I will not reign forever. Help me choose what comes after.

options.text: Suggest the sovereign need not step down.

examples: A reign that ends in a treaty is recast into The Alliance.
A reign that names no heir opens a Usurpation for someone else.

tropes.name: The Spoils

acts.title: The taken ground
acts.prompt: The war is won and {lost_other} is ours by right. Walk the ground and tell me what it is worth.

options.text: Strip it of anything that can be carried.

acts.title: The heir
acts.prompt: Someone of theirs survived and calls the ground stolen. Find out who.

options.text: Find the heir and hear the claim.
Find the heir and end the claim.

acts.title: The settlement
acts.prompt: Hold it, share it, or give it back. Advise me.

options.text: Hold the ground and garrison it.
Share it with the heir under terms.

examples: The heir is spared and given terms; the victor gains rival:spared and rests with a Pardon hook.
The ground is stripped and held; the heir's Revenge opens against the victor.

tropes.name: The Veteran

acts.title: The pay
acts.prompt: The war is over and the army still wants feeding. Find me the coin, or find me a reason to keep them.

options.text: Raise the coin from the city.
Keep the army under arms and find it work.

acts.title: The grievance
acts.prompt: The council thinks the war is done with me. Show them it is not.

options.text: Petition the seat on the veterans' behalf.
March the veterans to the hall.

acts.title: The disbanding
acts.prompt: Disband them, or crown me. There is no third road.

options.text: Disband the army and go home.
Take the seat with the army behind you.

examples: The army is disbanded and the warlord rests with a Succession hook as a mentor.
The army marches on the hall; the warlord is recast into Usurpation, then Tyranny.

tropes.name: The Peace

acts.title: The terms
acts.prompt: Another war would cost more than the last. Carry my terms to {realm_other} before the harvest.

acts.title: The hostage
acts.prompt: They want surety. Someone of mine must go to them.

options.text: Refuse the surety and prepare the walls.

acts.title: The seal
acts.prompt: Witness the peace, and remember who broke it if it breaks.

examples: The peace holds and the sovereign rests with an Alliance hook.
The surety is refused and the sovereign is recast into The Siege when the risk fires.

tropes.name: The Pursuit

acts.title: The rumour
acts.prompt: {rival} lives and calls what I took stolen. Find where they shelter.

acts.title: The corner
acts.prompt: Bring them to me, or bring me to them.

acts.title: The end of it
acts.prompt: The claim dies with them, or it dies with terms. Choose.

examples: The heir is spared; the warlord gains rival:spared and rests with a Pardon hook.
The heir dies; the warlord rests with a Tyranny hook and the mantle opens for the player.

tropes.name: The March

acts.title: The empty granary
acts.prompt: We cannot feed the winter and {realm_other} can. Count what we have and what the road can carry.

options.text: Count honestly and say how short it is.
Say it is worse than it is, to justify what comes.

acts.title: The envoy or the scout
acts.prompt: Ride the road to them. Come back with grain, or come back with their walls drawn.

acts.title: The march
acts.prompt: Terms or the sword. Decide before the frost.

options.text: Take the terms and feed the city.
Ration the city and take nothing.

examples: Terms are taken; the sovereign rests with a Peace hook and the neighbour with an Alliance hook.
The march goes out; next age the lottery draws the war the outlook forecast, and the neighbour was on The Siege.
